Question: A list of integers has mode \(32\) and mean \(22.\) The smallest number in the list is \(10.\) The median \(m\) of the list is a member of the list. If the list member \(m\) were replaced by \(m+10,\) the mean and median of the new list would be \(24\) and \(m+10,\) respectively. If \(m\) were instead replaced by \(m-8,\) the median of the new list would be \(m-4.\) What is \(m?\)
Solution:
Replacing one entry by a number 10 larger increases the total by 10. If the list has \(n\) entries, its mean increases by \(10/n\). Thus
\[
\frac{10}{n}=24-22=2,
\]
so there are five entries, whose original total is \(5\cdot22=110\).

Since 32 is the mode, it occurs at least twice. It cannot occur three times, because every entry is at least 10 and
\[
3\cdot32+2\cdot10=116>110.
\]
The other three entries sum to \(110-64=46\). One is 10, so the remaining two sum to 36. Each is at least 10 and hence at most 26, placing both below 32. We can therefore write the sorted list as
\[
10,\ x,\ m,\ 32,\ 32,
\qquad x+m=36.
\]

After replacing \(m\) by \(m-8\), the median is the largest of the three entries \(10,x,m-8\), namely \(\max\{x,m-8\}\). The specified median \(m-4\) is larger than \(m-8\), so it must equal \(x\). Consequently,
\[
x=m-4,
\qquad (m-4)+m=36,
\]
which gives \(m=20\).

The resulting list is \(10,16,20,32,32\). Replacing 20 by 30 gives mean 24 and median 30; replacing it by 12 gives median 16, which is \(20-4\). Thus \(\boxed{m=20}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
